OA-P2-2015-MJ::6::q6-c.prompt:
Mr Charleston, an angry customer, storms into Murrell Motors and the following conversation takes place between him and the customer service clerk.
Customer Service Clerk: Good morning Mr Charleston. May I help you?
Mr Charleston: This is nonsense! This is the second time in two months I’m in here with this car. It’s just two months old! You people don’t seem to know what you’re doing! A new car and it needs a part already! I was promised that someone would call me when the part came in and not a word have I heard from anyone!
Customer Service Clerk: Mr Charleston there’s no need for you to behave like that. After all it’s only a car. Besides we’ve been busy with other customers, and I have no idea when that part will be in. You’ll just have to wait.
Mr Charleston: What! The customer service in this place stinks! I demand to see the brand manager. I want my money back now! I’ll never do business with this company again!
(i) Identify THREE rules of good customer service relations which the customer service clerk at Murrell Motors failed to observe. (3 marks)

(ii) State THREE ways in which such actions will affect the company, if this clerk continues to deal with customers in the same manner Mr Charleston was treated. (3 marks)
(iii) Instead of removing the clerk from the job (firing) what THREE actions could the company take to improve this clerk’s handling of customers? (3 marks)
